title: Reading Test 1: The Growth of Urban Cycling
passage: In many large cities, cycling has changed from a leisure activity into a practical form of daily transport. This shift has been encouraged by rising fuel costs, crowded roads, and a growing awareness of environmental issues. City governments have also begun to redesign roads to make them safer for cyclists.

One of the most visible changes is the introduction of protected cycle lanes. Unlike painted lanes, protected lanes use physical barriers to separate cyclists from motor vehicles. Supporters argue that this makes cycling feel safer and encourages beginners to try travelling by bike. However, these lanes can be expensive to build, and they sometimes reduce the amount of road space available to cars and buses.

Bike-sharing schemes have also become common in urban areas. These schemes allow users to rent a bicycle for a short period and return it at another location. In theory, they make cycling more convenient because people do not need to own or maintain a bicycle. In practice, their success depends on careful planning. If bikes are not available near homes, stations, and workplaces, people are unlikely to use the service regularly.

Researchers have found that cycling infrastructure can bring wider benefits. Regular cycling may improve public health, reduce local air pollution, and lower pressure on public transport systems. Nevertheless, the benefits are not distributed equally. In some cities, new cycling routes are concentrated in wealthier districts, while areas with poorer transport links receive less investment.

The future of urban cycling is likely to depend on whether cities can treat it as part of a wider transport system rather than as a separate activity. Better connections between cycling routes, train stations, bus stops, and pedestrian areas could make short journeys easier and reduce dependence on private cars. For this reason, many planners now view cycling as a key element of sustainable urban mobility.

questionGroups.title: Questions 1-4
questionGroups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information in the passage? Choose TRUE, FALSE, or NOT GIVEN.

questions.question: Cycling is now used as a practical form of transport in many large cities.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 1 states that cycling has changed into a practical form of daily transport in many large cities.

questions.question: Protected cycle lanes are cheaper to build than painted cycle lanes.
questions.explanation: The passage says protected lanes can be expensive, but it does not directly compare their cost with painted lanes.

questions.question: Bike-sharing schemes remove the need for users to own or maintain a bicycle.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 3 says users do not need to own or maintain a bicycle.

questions.question: All districts receive equal investment in cycling infrastructure.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 4 says the benefits are not distributed equally and some areas receive less investment.

questionGroups.title: Questions 5-7
questionGroups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C, or D.

questions.question: What is one reason city governments have encouraged cycling?

options.text: A reduction in the price of cars
A growing awareness of environmental issues
A lack of interest in public health

questions.explanation: Paragraph 1 mentions environmental awareness as one reason for the shift towards cycling.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is a possible problem with protected cycle lanes?

options.text: They cannot be used by beginners
They make roads more dangerous for cyclists
They may reduce space for cars and buses
They are illegal in many cities

questions.explanation: Paragraph 2 says protected lanes sometimes reduce road space available to cars and buses.

questions.question: What does the final paragraph suggest about the future of urban cycling?

options.text: It should be separated from all other forms of transport
It depends on better integration with wider transport systems
It is only useful in wealthy districts

questions.explanation: The final paragraph says cycling should be treated as part of a wider transport system.

questionGroups.title: Questions 8-10
questionGroups.instructions: Answer the questions below. Write no more than two words from the passage for each answer.

questions.question: What type of cycle lanes use physical barriers?
questions.explanation: Paragraph 2 explains that protected cycle lanes use physical barriers.

questions.question: What systems may experience less pressure as a result of cycling infrastructure?
questions.explanation: Paragraph 4 says cycling infrastructure may lower pressure on public transport systems.

questions.question: What type of urban mobility is cycling described as part of?
questions.explanation: The final sentence describes cycling as a key element of sustainable urban mobility.
